title: The Day Before the Winter Solstice
markdown:
Somehow another year is almost over. Yesterday the building manager sent a warm little notice:

> Warm ginger tea, on the house — comfort doesn't take a day off.
>
> Property team · Convenience from the heart, service in the doing
>
> A cup of hot ginger tea 🍵 to start a full day
>
> Pickup: Dec 20, 8:30 a.m.
>
> Locations: East and south gates of the compound
>
> Looking forward to seeing you 🌹

So Winter Solstice is almost here. Same thing last year — staff handing out ginger tea at the gate. The feeling was different this time. Last year it felt surprising, almost ceremonial. This year it just felt thoughtful. I had to take a cup. After my wife took one, I said thank you.

This has been a year of feeling a lot:

- How long can things hold if the broader climate keeps getting harder?
- Is there still trust between people?
- Can you even eat this stuff?
- Look both ways — carefully — when you cross the street

The more of that there is, the more I notice small kindness nearby. So I keep a real respect for the property staff.

It's also been a year of wanting to write more — and still not updating the blog. The root reason is simple and a little embarrassing: other people write so well, and my stuff feels like a diary. I second-guess titles, second-guess the body, wonder if it's too rambling, if anyone would care. Just now I was stuck on the title. It says *The Day Before the Winter Solstice*, but only the first paragraph is about that day — then I kept cutting and rewriting. Suddenly it clicked: why am I editing this into something else? Just write what's true right now. Write it the way it is.

Back to the ginger tea. I used to gloss over details like this. This year I don't. Especially outside your usual circles, with people you barely know — a little trust is rare, and worth noticing.

That's enough for today. A decent place to start.
